description.narrative: The Output is created for the development and implementation of Disaster Risk Reduction Program

condition.narrative: UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

description.narrative: 1.1. Organize consultations with relevant agencies at the country level to integrate preparedness programmes and drills into the annual school curriculum. 1.2. Support the schools in reviewing their preparedness plans, drill scenarios, Standard Operating Procedures and evacuation routes and ensure all relevant materials and tools are available in local language as required. 1.3. Evaluate the drills organized by the schools on a designated annual day. 1.4. Drive commitments by local governments to cost-share and allocate annual resources for school preparedness activities. 1.5. Continue to feature project activities on the microsite including events around World Tsunami Awareness Day. 1.6 Support activities around Tonga Rock. 2.1. Develop new partnerships with local governments, private sector, academic institutions, media agencies and local communities that substantially help to scale up the preparedness programmes and drills in countries. 2.2. Organize Training of Trainers for schools. 2.3. Support the further development of STEP A for universal applicability in multiple countries and for multiple hazards 2.4. Support five new countries in Asia-Pacific to organize preparedness programmes and drills based on lessons learnt and good practice guidelines under phase 1. 2.5. Produce stories, blogs and videos featuring the drills on the project microsite and promote on social media. 3.1. Deploy experts to countries requiring support on data collection.

comment.narrative: Output 1: School preparedness and awareness programmes for tsunamis institutionalised in project countries. Output 2: School preparedness and awareness programmes for tsunamis replicated and adapted in more schools in Asia-Pacific. Output 3: Support project countries to enhance their capacity for data collection

Programme module will be distributed to 16 countries in December for contextualized. 2.2 At least 3 policy briefs developed and disseminated (1 per country) • This is planning to implement December to February. 2.3 Regional Guide updated and disseminated • This is planning to implement December to February. 3.1 At least 4 key events marked with digital communications • Palau has implemented Tsunami drill with Kayangel Island in September which is disaster preparedness month in Palau. Video was produced with message from NEMO Executive Director, school principal, students and residents who participated the drill. Subtitles of video were translated into Japanese and released SNS of Tokyo RO to introduce UNDPs work in Pacific country. • On World Tsunami Awareness Day 2022, BRH is collaborating with UNDRR and ESCAP to organize an event ‘Early Warning and Early Action Before Every Tsunami’, invited officials from the Embassy of Japan as a representative of a project’s donor. Also, UNDP BRH invited project’s counterparts such as officials from Ministry of Education in Fiji, Palau and Solomon Islands to participate open discussion of the event. • On World Tsunami Awareness Day 2022, UNDP Thailand is organizing an event ‘Role of Parliamentarians to Reduce Disaster Risks in Thailand’, BRH invited officials from the Embassy of Japan as a representative of a project’s donor. This event is planning to hold as a hybrid, mixing of online participation and onsite. After the event, UNDP Thailand publish video clip with highlighting of the event for public. 3.2 At least two events are organised to promote DRR education for children and communities • BRH has published Tsunami Story Books which is a series of illustrated real-life stories from the Asia-Pacific region that aims to help children better understand the magnitude of a tsunami and how to be prepared. 1st story from Solomon Islands, 2nd one is from Thailand, 3rd one is from Indonesia and 4th is from Tonga. 5th story from Japan in under preparing. • Vietnam is working to produce animation video as a disaster preparedness material for children, they’re also aiming to release animation with a event such as quiz contest in school or community. • UNDP Thailand is preparing the video and posters will be used as educational tools for what they have conducted National Guidelines and ToTs. These materials will be launched on 5th November and 26th December, respectively.

Over 100,000 students, teachers and school administration trained in tsunami education and safe evacuation drills, raising the total to 150,000 from 23 countries across two phases of the regional tsunami project. Key results in 2020 included: five countries institutionalized annual school tsunami preparedness; two local governments committed to cost-share tsunami preparedness activities; 24 videos, 4 newsletters and articles promoted visibility and awareness of tsunami preparedness efforts and World Tsunami Awareness Day promoted at high level events. In collaboration with UNDRR, a checklist for school administrators on tsunami evacuation during COVID-19 was developed based on lessons learned from Japan.
